A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M4-SAR, MSRODet, and E2E-OSDet. All pages, including v1 Appendices A–D, are readable. V2 incorporates much appendix material into the main text and omits other material; these are identifiable document changes, not extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original M4-SAR detection experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative results in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original M4-SAR experiments and adds evaluations on OGSOD-1.0 and OGSOD-2.0 in Table IV.

M1.justification: The FAM augmentation, interleaved CMIM processing, AFM fusion, and composite loss from v1 Appendix C are retained in v2 Section IV. Revised notation and architecture drawings do not change the procedure. The revised parameter count is not accompanied by an identified architectural modification.

E1.justification: V1's experimental evaluation is confined to M4-SAR. V2 Section VI-A and Table IV add optical-only, SAR-only, and fusion evaluations on OGSOD-1.0 and OGSOD-2.0, substantially extending benchmark coverage. M4-SAR's six categories and represented environmental conditions remain.

E2.justification: Relative to v1 Table 2, v2 Table II adds YOLOv12 as an optical-only and SAR-only baseline and COMO as a fusion comparator. The existing M4-SAR comparator set is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The added OGSOD experiments specify 300 epochs and 256×256 inputs, introducing settings for the new evaluations. Existing M4-SAR training budgets, optimizers, input resolution, and metrics remain unchanged. The stated dataset total changes from 112,184 to 112,174 pairs, without explaining whether this corrects a count or reflects changed data.

E4.justification: V2 Table III adds parameter costs to the retained component ablation. Core filter, scanning, and hyperparameter analyses remain, but additional SSIM examples and the supplementary detection comparisons from v1 Appendix D are omitted. Grad-CAM examples decrease from twelve rows in v1 Figure 14 to four in v2 Figure 9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability, or significance tests. V2's added experiments retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds OGSOD results, including E2E-OSDet mAP values of 67.3 and 65.1, and new M4-SAR results for YOLOv12 and COMO. Existing M4-SAR detection scores, including E2E-OSDet's 61.4 mAP, remain unchanged. Its reported parameter count changes from 27.5M to 24.7M; KFIoU and ablation parameter counts are newly supplied. Some appendix SSIM and qualitative results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 restates the augmentation, sequence interleaving, scanning, fusion, and loss equations from v1 Appendix C with revised notation. No substantive mathematical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: V2 softens the dataset priority claim from the first comprehensive optical-SAR fusion dataset to a new or novel dataset in the abstract and introduction. The toolkit contribution, E2E-OSDet's claimed domain-gap mitigation, and the claimed 5.7-point mAP advantage remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting class imbalance to coastal infrastructure prevalence and harbor extent, and interprets the OGSOD results as evidence of generalizability. It removes v1's limitation concerning unreliable optical-guided annotations under occlusion or blurred boundaries. Temporal misalignment, restricted categories, and deployment cost remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix A's normalized quadrilateral .txt annotation specification and CC BY 4.0 declaration, plus Appendix D's explicit YOLOv11-S and FP16 details. It newly documents cloud-free annotation followed by substitution with corresponding cloudy images, and supplies basic OGSOD training settings. These substantially change dataset-use and reproduction documentation; the public code/data link remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including MSOD, SARATR-X, and COMO, while removing several handcrafted-feature, missing-modality, and lightweight-network references. It expands discussion of OGSOD-2.0, whose underlying paper was already cited in v1. The central positioning around optical-SAR dataset scarcity and modality discrepancies remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively reorganizes the narrative: appendix related work and detailed method descriptions become main Sections II and IV, experimental details are consolidated, and discussion is restructured. Related-work prose is substantially rewritten, while dataset appendix sections and parts of the supplementary discussion are removed.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the dataset pipeline and category-statistics displays, and merges v1 Figures 4–5 into one architecture figure. Scanning and selected heatmap visuals move into the main text, other appendix figures disappear, existing tables are reformatted, and Table IV is added.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens comparisons and integrates method explanations, but removes useful dataset-format, licensing, and supplementary documentation. The added OGSOD evidence is difficult to assess because v2 describes SAR-only test sets yet reports optical/fusion testing without explaining the adaptation. New Table III also contains inconsistent parameter arithmetic, such as 14.17M + 5.68M versus 19.01M. These unresolved issues and documentation losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
